verses.text: He built the altar of burnt offering out of acacia wood. It was square, about two and a quarter metres long and two and a quarter metres wide, and about one and a third metres high.
He made a horn at each of its four corners, so that the horns and the altar were one piece. He covered the altar with bronze.
He made all the altar's tools out of bronze: its pots, shovels, bowls, meat forks, and fire pans.
He made a grate for the altar, a bronze net, and put it under the ledge of the altar, so that it reached halfway up.
He cast four bronze rings for the four corners of the bronze grate, to hold the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with bronze.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it. He made the altar hollow, out of boards.
He made the bronze washing bowl and its bronze stand from the bronze mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Then he made the courtyard. The south side was forty-five metres long, with curtains of fine twisted linen.
It had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The north side was also forty-five metres long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The west end was twenty-two metres wide, with curtains, ten posts, and ten bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The east end, towards the sunrise, was also twenty-two metres wide.
On one side of the entrance there were curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.
On the other side of the entrance to the courtyard there were also curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.
All the curtains around the courtyard were made of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were covered with silver. All the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

The screen for the entrance to the courtyard was made of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns. It was nine metres long and over two metres high, the same as the curtains of the courtyard.
It had four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks and bands were silver, and their tops were covered with silver.
All the tent pegs of the holy tent and of the courtyard around it were bronze.
These are the amounts of the materials used for the holy tent, the Tent of the Covenant. They were recorded at Moses' command by the Levites, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. He was a carver and a designer, and he sewed beautiful patterns in blue, purple, and red yarn and fine linen.
All the gold given as an offering and used for the work on the holy place weighed about one thousand kilograms, by the weight of the holy place.
The silver given by those in the community who were counted weighed about three thousand four hundred kilograms, by the weight of the holy place.

This was one beka, half a shekel, for each person, by the weight of the holy place. It was given by everyone who was counted, twenty years old or more, six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men.
About three thousand four hundred kilograms of silver was used to cast the bases for the holy place and for the curtain, one hundred bases, about thirty-four kilograms for each base.
He used the remaining twenty kilograms of silver to make the hooks for the posts, to cover the tops of the posts, and to make their bands.
The bronze given as an offering weighed about two thousand four hundred kilograms.
He used it to make the bases for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grate and all its tools,
the bases for the courtyard all around and for its entrance, and all the tent pegs for the holy tent and for the courtyard around it.
